scope: Synthetic 100M sphere-placement benchmark; distinct from detector/Rust/raw supplement
review_findings: Four 25M texture pairs preserve global input stream and original shader/reference. All targets synchronized.
Six fresh browser pipelines each retain all100M RGBA outputs, stop the continuous timer, then validate all300M XYZ coordinates.
Final resident/streaming browser output validated once, not every resident trial.
Both NumPy runs validate final resident and all three cold outputs with independent algebraic FP64 oracle.
Native GPU,CPU1,multicore each validate all300M coordinates after every one of10 trials on each Mac.
Native M4 source,binary,fixtures and final-output hashes independently rechecked; fixtures identical to supplied M5 fixtures.
provenance_limits: M5 native source/shader/fixture/result hashes and reproduction commands supplied, but no contemporaneous compile log or binary hash tying that historical executable to the source. Numerical output validation passes; executable provenance is weaker than M4.

M5 resident browser uses v2 export; M4 resident uses v3 page. The complete resident GPU class, timing method, shader, input generator and reference are byte-identical; v3 adds a separate cold-pipeline action. Both cold exports match the same complete v3 manifest.
Normal desktop conditions, different total memory and existing M4 swap prevent isolated chip-speed inference. Browser readback difference is unexplained.
FP64 NumPy XYZ,FP32 native XYZ and FP32 padded browser RGBA have different precision/layout/cadence. Validation and process/context startup are excluded where documented.
